title: Is This a Good Time for Active Management? | Dimensional
gist: Dimensional tests whether high cross-sectional dispersion helps stock pickers: across 2006–2025 US active equity funds underperformed benchmarks by about 10 bps/month even in high-dispersion months, so mispricing opportunity does not rise with dispersion — though active flexibility may help execution when volatility lifts trading costs.

insights.claim: Cross-sectional dispersion in US stock returns has been unusually high recently — average dispersion over the 12 months ending April 2026 was at the 95th percentile of rolling one-year periods since January 2006.
insights.speaker: Wes Crill, PhD, Senior Client Solutions Director and Vice President
insights.so_what: Sets up the common claim that conditions favor stock pickers.

insights.claim: In months with above-median US cross-sectional dispersion from 2006–2025, active US equity funds underperformed their prospectus benchmarks by about 10 basis points per month in aggregate, a slightly larger shortfall than in low-dispersion months, so high dispersion does not create low-hanging fruit for active managers.
insights.speaker: Wes Crill, PhD, Senior Client Solutions Director and Vice President
insights.so_what: The 'dispersion is high, so now is the time for stock picking' narrative has no empirical support in this test.
insights.quote: The results show little evidence there's more low-hanging fruit for active managers in high dispersion months.

insights.claim: High volatility periods tend to bring higher trade costs, so strategies that track indices may impose higher costs on investors when volatility escalates, while a flexible active process is potentially most valuable for execution during such times.
insights.speaker: Wes Crill, PhD, Senior Client Solutions Director and Vice President
insights.so_what: The case for flexible implementation, rather than alpha from mispricing, is stronger when markets are turbulent.
insights.locator: Does this mean active management is not beneficial

insights.claim: If the goal is finding mispriced securities, now is probably not a good time for active management — or ever — but if the goal is better execution when things go haywire, the answer may be yes.
insights.speaker: Wes Crill, PhD, Senior Client Solutions Director and Vice President
insights.so_what: Reframes the active-vs-passive debate around execution flexibility, not selection skill.
insights.quote: If your objective is to find mispriced securities, probably not now—or ever.

source_meta.author: Wes Crill, PhD, Senior Client Solutions Director and Vice President
